text:
Unifying clean water customer journeys and automating regulatory reporting at Yorkshire Water.
Aiimi Facebook link
Aiimi Twitter/X link
Aiimi LinkedIn link

Across two strategic projects at Yorkshire Water, Aiimi consolidated clean water interaction data and automated reporting for the 23 Performance Commitments – critical regulatory measures that directly impact financial penalties and rewards for water companies.

The Problem  
Yorkshire Water faced significant challenges with fragmented visibility of customer journeys and the manual, error-prone tracking of regulatory Performance Commitments, using Ofwat’s rigorous definitions.

In Customer Experience Management, disparate manual reporting and a disjointed customer journey, managed across 4+ fragmented source systems and 7+ business areas, resulting in poor governance and a lack of trust in the data. This made it difficult for the Customer Service teams and Operational Managers to make informed resource decisions, manage performance, share best practice, or establish and track KPIs.   

In Performance Commitment Reporting, manually tracking the 23 Performance Commitments was a substantial operational burden. Reporting was inconsistent across departments and calculations of Outcome Delivery Incentives were manual and error-prone, resulting in splintered sources and inconsistent measures being reported to executive teams.  Under regulatory scrutiny, these errors and inconsistencies led to millions in unforeseen costs.  

The Solution  
Aiimi partnered with Yorkshire Water to modernise their data landscape and regulatory management, creating a ‘single source of truth’ for operational efficiency and automated reporting. We delivered a suite of reports to ensure insights can be seen by the teams doing the work and used to accurately inform executive-level decision-making.  

In Customer Experience Management, we designed and deployed consolidated customer journey dashboards, spanning four key customer journeys and drawing from multiple disparate data sources and business areas. These dashboards surface near-real-time data to support operational decision-making, delivering insights across eight KPIs, with the ability to drill-down into the data across 18 key drivers. Subject Matter Experts can interrogate the data, identify where customers are slipping through the net, and direct resource to areas that need it most.   

In Performance Commitment reporting, Aiimi built an end-to-end reporting framework for the 23 regulatory measures, taking Ofwat’s complex calculations and translating them into automated data-engineering logic. By embedding the regulatory definitions directly into reporting processes, we enabled the system to not only calculate current forecast positions but also surface predictive forecasting and current financial positions. This provides executive teams with an accurate, governed, assured, and data-rich report to inform decision-making.

The Result   
Aiimi has delivered tangible commercial value across both projects, solving problems that are common and increasingly urgent in the utilities sector: fragmented data, high regulatory risk, and limited confidence in reporting. Yorkshire Water has shifted from reactive, manual processes towards governed, predictive, and scalable performance management, laying the foundations for a more proactive approach.  

One version of the truth: Disparate data sources and inconsistent reporting were brought together in a consolidated, governed data foundation, enabling a shared and trusted view of the customer journey and regulatory performance. Operational teams and leaders are aligned around the same assured metrics for Clean Water, reducing duplication and manual effort while strengthening confidence and decision-making.  

Lower operational costs through better visibility: Near-real‑time customer journey insights enable teams to identify pressure points, repeat contacts, and service failures early. This supports targeted resourcing, faster intervention, and improved customer outcomes, reducing the operational cost of poor service without increasing headcount or reporting burden.  

Early warning of financial exposure: Surfacing predictive forecasting against Outcome Delivery Incentives gives leadership teams clear visibility of risks and opportunities earlier in the reporting cycle. It provides an audit trail and reduces misreporting and the associated multimillion-pound penalties. Executives can now take corrective action before year-end, rather than reacting to issues after the financial impact has been felt.  

Increased confidence at operational and board levels: With a single, auditable, and assured reporting framework, leaders across the organisation have confidence that performance positions are accurate, consistent, and defensible. This strengthens governance, supports regulatory challenge, and enables strategic decision‑making.  

By unifying data and automating regulatory reporting, Aiimi has empowered Yorkshire Water to move from fragmented, reactive management to a proactive, data-driven culture – delivering greater efficiency, reduced risk, and more effective regulatory compliance.

Richard Heighington
